restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r3-prefix-v1 only (three partial rounds 4, 5 and 6 plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction uses the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

time_log2 is the operation count of the algorithm (one centre, K = 1, isolation at its 64-round cap, one thread) plus the 1,000,000-op offline bound, declared preprocessing_log2 = 20, inside time_log2. Stage C: value-domain Montgomery powering on truncated point sets, 477 of the 512 depth-9 nodes of the subgroup of order 2^20 and of its coset (n' = 976,896; bradcush b30de9bf/a41aecdd, proof.md 4.3T), passes 3 | 4, 4, 3, 3 | 3 on the 18-word register file (no R-REG64, ruling 867c60fd), row 61,516,769,663; stage D: the inversion-free half-gcd on three rows (bradcush 4bcabff8, proof.md 4.4) charged for the normal remainder sequence with the quotient and return tests and the ABORT on any other case (bradcush e6dcb600, proof.md 6.3, 9.5), row 17,835,006,021; an abnormal trial ABORTs after a prefix of the work, so the time bound holds for every sequence. N_max = 80,597,497,306. Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 279.

memory_log2_bytes = 26.990 is the footprint: the arena is the capacity of the two-ended allocator of proof.md 4.2 on the allocation/free sequence of the trial, its high-water mark 127,877,376 bytes reached in stage C (stage D, with the bump arena of its half-gcd, peaks at 104,997,056; an abnormal trial ABORTs after a prefix of these allocations), two-ended pool 127,877,376 + 128 bytes and stages E and later 16,896 bytes = 127,894,400 bytes, plus 5,250,444 bytes of code and static data and a 65,536-byte stack, 133,210,380 bytes = 2^26.990, rounded up at three decimals (proof.md 7; reproduced event by event in Appendix E). No stored advice; each twiddle table is built at run time by the stage that uses it and charged in that stage's row (proof.md 4.2).

success_probability 0.39009 is a probability over the algorithm's fresh independent uniform 256-bit random words (two per field element, (w1 2^256 + w2) mod p, proof.md 4.1.1) for the fixed target, derived from the premises H-ONE and H-NORMAL as 1 - (1 - q + delta)^K - K (eps_coin + eps_iso + eps_g) = q - delta - eps_coin - eps_iso - eps_g with K = 1, q = 0.3931 (H-ONE, proof.md 9.1), delta = 0.003 (H-NORMAL, proof.md 9.5), eps_iso <= 2.371e-15, eps_coin <= 65 p/2^512 <= 1.404e-76 and eps_g <= n'(D - 1)/p < 2^-213 (the centre makes g_c vanish on O1, where stage C inverts g), all proved (proof.md 4.1.1, 4.3T, 9.2, 9.4). The value is 0.390099999999997628 (>= the organizer floor 0.39), claimed floored at five decimals. Stage D is charged for the normal remainder sequence with the ABORT (proof.md 6.3); H-NORMAL enters only this bound, not the time or memory. Stage C reproduces R = S^((p-1)/2) mod g exactly (Montgomery products on the truncated point sets, proof.md 4.3T, no premise).

heuristics.statement: Notation: p is the Pallas prime, D = 5^9, F in F_p[X] the fixed digest polynomial of proof.md section 2.3 at r = 3 (degree D), g_c the monic odd part of F about the centre c (proof.md section 3, degree m = 976,562), k(c) the number of nonzero squares S with g_c(S) = 0 (k(c) = deg G of stage D). Premise: the number of centres c in F_p with 1 <= k(c) <= 16 is at least 0.3931 p; equivalently, for c uniform on F_p, P(1 <= k(c) <= 16) >= q = 0.3931. With H-NORMAL (delta = 0.003) and one centre (K = 1) the success bound is q - delta - eps_coin - eps_iso - eps_g = 0.390099999999997628 (proof.md 9.2). The value 0.3931 is 0.0003693 below 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.3934693, the probability that a uniform signed permutation (the hyperoctahedral group B_m, the monodromy of the cover G(c,t) = g_c(t^2) = 0 at the depths where it is computed) has a positive fixed point, and below the four-moment Bonferroni bound 151/384 = 0.3932292 (proof.md 9.1, 9.3). The allowance split between H-ONE and H-NORMAL follows cryptogakusei's entry 4888e783.
heuristics.scope: The fixed Poseidon target poseidon-orchard-r3-prefix-v1, this line construction (the line j = 0 of the first two rounds, odd part about a centre, proof.md sections 2-3), the polynomial F of proof.md section 2.3; centres uniform on F_p. Not claimed for other round counts. The other terms of the success bound are H-NORMAL (proof.md 9.5) and proved terms: the coin bias, the isolation lemma and g_c nonzero on O1 (proof.md 4.1.1, 9.4, 4.3T); the time and memory bounds do not depend on the premise.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the law of k(c) at reduced depth to the polynomial F of depth 9. The roots of G(c,t) in t are +-t_1, ..., +-t_m, so the monodromy group of the cover lies in the hyperoctahedral group B_m and k(c) counts the positive fixed points of the Frobenius element; for the full group B_m this number is Poisson(1/2) in the limit, P(k >= 1) = 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.3934693 (exactly 1 - sum_{j<=m} (-1/2)^j/j!), and Bonferroni at order 4 gives P >= 151/384 = 0.3932292 from four moments (proof.md 9.3). At N = 2 and 3 S-box layers on the deployed constants and the line of this construction the arithmetic monodromy is B_12 and B_62 (Grok jobs 136 and 137, re-run on the deployed constants, proof.md 10.3); the geometric monodromy then contains the commutator subgroup of B_m, the j-fold fibre powers are absolutely irreducible, and the Aubry-Perret bound with Bonferroni gives 0.39346933 <= P(1 <= k <= 16) <= 0.39346944 there: the premise is a theorem at those depths. Measured: toy fields at p = 1,048,627, exact over all centres, 27 cases with 3 to 8 layers, P(k >= 1) between 0.39214 and 0.39436; the organizer-run tests one-centre-n2-t256 and one-centre-n3-t24 run one trial of the algorithm at depth N = 2, 3 (m = 12, 62) per organizer seed and return a witness pair exactly when the sequence is normal, 1 <= k(c) <= 16 and the isolated root gives a verified collision of F_N, with expected count about 0.393469 T under H-ONE (proof.md 10.5.1), an observation with no interval inferred; in our local runs of euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a to -f the gcd had positive degree at 1,229 of 3,072 centres (0.400). The deviations from the law shrink like p^(-1/2) and do not grow with the degree (toy fields 1.36/sqrt(p); the counts of Grok job 139, eps ~ 3.1/sqrt(p) over degrees 5 to 1,953,125); the premise extrapolates the law to N = 9 with an allowance stated exactly as 0.0003693.
heuristics.limitations: It concerns this F, not every polynomial of degree D: it is false for permutation polynomials (k = 0 at every centre) and for a decomposable F with imprimitive monodromy, and false at one layer (m = 2: the law gives exactly 0.375). At N = 9 the monodromy is not computed and the counts N_3, N_4 are out of reach of Weil's bound; the premise is the extrapolation of a law that is a theorem at N = 2, 3 and measured on toy fields and on the real field at N <= 4. The allowance 0.0003693 is thin; the organizer-run counts test the construction at m = 12 and 62, not its scale. The value-domain stage C adds no premise (the Montgomery products on the truncated point sets are exact, proof.md 4.3T); the inversion-free stage D computes the same remainder sequence and the same gcd up to scalars.

heuristics.statement: For the centre c uniform on F_p, the Euclidean remainder sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1), where g_c is the monic odd part of proof.md section 3 (degree m = 976,562) and R_c = S^((p-1)/2) mod g_c, is normal down to its gcd (deg(R_c - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient has degree 1) except with probability at most delta = 0.003 (2^-8.38). Stage D is charged for the normal sequence; every division tests its quotient degree and every call of the half-gcd its return, and on any other case the trial ends (ABORT, proof.md 4.4, 6.3). With H-ONE (q = 0.3931) and one centre (K = 1) the success bound is q - delta - eps_coin - eps_iso - eps_g = 0.390099999999997628 (proof.md 9.2).
heuristics.scope: The pairs (g_c, R_c - 1) of the target poseidon-orchard-r3-prefix-v1, c uniform on F_p. It enters only the success probability: the time and memory bounds hold for every remainder sequence, because a trial with an abnormal sequence ends at its first failed test after executing a prefix of the charged work (proof.md 6.3). Not claimed for other round counts. The premise is bradcush's (entries e6dcb600 and 1aa56884); the allowance delta = 0.003 follows cryptogakusei's split (4888e783) and the organizer-run tests follow gta6rp's form (bef31fdd).
heuristics.extrapolation: For a uniformly random pair of degrees m and m - 1 the sequence is abnormal exactly when one of the m principal subresultant coefficients vanishes, each a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 2m in the coefficients, so by Schwartz-Zippel the probability is at most 2 m^2 / p < 2^-213; the premise extrapolates a much weaker form of this random-pair behaviour (delta = 0.003) to the structured pair (g_c, R_c - 1). Measured support, organizer-run (proof.md 10.5.1): the six experiments euclid-normal-n2-t256-l2-a to -f compute the complete Euclidean sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1) for this construction on the truncation F_2 of the digest polynomial (proof.md 10.3; m = 12) for 256 organizer-seeded trials of two centres each (3,072 sequences in all) and return a witness pair exactly when both sequences of a trial are normal; euclid-normal-n3-t24 and euclid-normal-n4-t2 do the same at m = 62, 312. The prediction is that every computed sequence is normal; zero abnormal in the 3,072 sequences is a reproducible observation consistent with the premise; the organizer-seeded centres are not treated as independent unselected samples and no population bound is drawn from them (delta = 0.003 is the declared premise). Our local runs of the six entries in the organizer's container settings: 3,072 sequences, all normal.
heuristics.limitations: Not verified at r = 3, which would need the computation itself. The Schwartz-Zippel bound does not transfer, because the coefficients of R_c have degree about p in those of g_c; an algebraic relation between g_c and R_c that forces a principal subresultant coefficient to vanish for many centres would invalidate the premise, and none is known. The success bound stays at least 0.39 for every delta <= 0.0030999 at q = 0.3931 (proof.md 9.2), above the stated delta = 0.003. The organizer-run tests are at m = 12 to 312, far below m: they test the construction, not its scale; normality is computed inside the submitted program and the runner checks only the returned witness pairs.
